title: A corticohypothalamic circuit that mediates maternal awakening to pup cries
title_zh: 介导母鼠对幼崽哭声觉醒的皮质下丘脑电路
abstract: Maternal caregiving requires sensory vigilance to ensure offspring survival, particularly during sleep. Infant cries are salient sensory cues that reliably trigger maternal arousal and caregiving responses in both humans and dams, but the underlying neural circuitry remains poorly defined. Here we identify a corticohypothalamic circuit in mice that mediates maternal awakening in response to pup calls. We show that layer 6 (L6) neurons in the temporal association cortex and ectorhinal cortex (TeA/Ect) projecting to the preoptic area (POA) exhibit enhanced responsiveness to pup calls after the transition to motherhood. This enhanced responsiveness is mediated by increased expression of dopamine receptor D1 (Drd1) in TeA/Ect → POA neurons. Additionally, we reveal a pathway from the auditory thalamus to L6 TeA/Ect neurons that transmits pup cues during sleep. Together, these findings identify a dedicated neural circuit that grants infant cries privileged access to arousal systems, likely representing a fundamental adaptation for caregiving across mammals.
abstract_zh: 母性照顾需要感官警觉以确保后代存活，特别是在睡眠期间。幼崽哭声是显著的感官线索，能可靠地在人类和母鼠中触发觉醒和照顾行为，但其背后的神经电路尚不明确。本研究在小鼠中鉴定出一条介导母性对幼崽叫声觉醒的皮质下丘脑电路。我们发现，在母性转变后，颞关联皮质和耳后皮质（TeA/耳区）第6层（L6）神经元投射至前视下丘脑（POA）时，对幼崽叫声的响应性增强。这种增强的响应性由TeA/耳区→POA神经元中多巴胺受体D1（Drd1）表达量的增加介导。此外，我们还揭示了一条从听觉丘脑至L6 TeA/耳区神经元的路径，在睡眠期间传输幼崽线索。这些发现共同确定了一个专门的神经电路，使幼崽哭声能获得觉醒系统的优先通道，这可能代表了哺乳动物照顾的基本适应性特征。
